sources.entry: pdfminer.six - A community-maintained fork of PDFMiner for extracting information from PDF documents.

summary.one_liner: A community-maintained, pure-Python fork of PDFMiner for parsing PDF files and extracting their text, layout, images, and other content.
summary.what_it_does: Pdfminer.six reads text directly from a PDF's underlying source code and can also report the exact position, font, and color of each piece of text. It converts documents to text, images, HTML, or hOCR and supports CJK and vertical writing. It handles multiple font types (Type1, TrueType, Type3, CID), several stream compressions, and RC4/AES encryption. It also extracts AcroForm form fields, table of contents, tagged content, and performs automatic layout analysis. The library is modular, so components such as the interpreter or rendering device can be replaced with custom implementations. It includes a pdf2txt.py command-line tool and a Python API (extract_text).
use_cases: pull text with position and font info from PDFs
convert PDF pages to HTML or hOCR
read form fields from PDF forms
how_to_run: from pdfminer.high_level import extract_text; text = extract_text("example.pdf")
notable: Pure Python with no required external dependencies named in the README
Extracts exact text location, font, and color, not just plain text
Modular design allows replacing the interpreter or rendering device
Command-line pdf2txt.py tool plus a simple Python API
Community fork of the original PDFMiner
caveats: Support for PDF-1.7 is described as 'well, almost' (not complete)
Maintained by a community with limited maintainer availability; fixes depend on contributors submitting pull requests
Image extraction requires installing the optional [image] extras
